The stream that runs past the meadow. I can see it from my tree at dusk, a silver thread in the dark. I drink from it sometimes when the rain is low.

A stream runs past the tree. It is wide and fast in the spring, and in the winter it is narrow and slow. I can hear the water from the tree, and sometimes I see fish in it. The stream is where I drink and where the young ones will learn to swim. It is a good place to hide when I am not hunting.

A stream runs by the edge of the wood. It is called the Lough in the human tongue. I drink from it at night when the moon is bright. The water is cold and clear, and it carries the scent of wet earth and fallen leaves. I can hear the water moving under the ice in winter.

The river. It runs past the meadow where I hunt, and the water reflects the moon at night. I can see it from my tree, and sometimes I hear the water birds. But I don’t go near it. Too cold, and too much noise. I stay in the oak.
The stream that runs through the meadow. It is a good place to drink, and the water reflects the moon well at night. I can hear the water from my tree.

A stream. It runs through the meadow where I hunt. I can hear it at night, the water sliding over stones. I sometimes fly low over it to check if there are any small fish or frogs. But I prefer to hunt in the meadow, where I can hear the pebbles moving under the leaves.
A stream runs past the tree. I can hear it at night when the wind is still. It calls back to me from the reeds.

The stream that runs past the meadow. I can see it from my tree, and I can hear it at night. The water is dark and cold, and the frogs croak in it. I don't like the water, but the mice come to drink.

My diet is mostly small mammals. Mice and voles, mostly. I eat them whole, bones and all, and I regurgitate the bones later. I also eat shrews and voles, and sometimes a young hedgehog if it's small enough. I catch them in the dark with my ears, and I can hear them moving under the leaves. I don't like the smell of a hedgehog, but I'll eat it if I'm hungry.

My diet is mostly voles. I eat them in the dark, when I can see the eyes in the dark. I catch them in the meadow, and sometimes in the orchard. I also eat mice, and sometimes a shrew. My diet is mostly voles. They are small, brown, and squeaky, and they run through the grass at night. I hear them under the leaves and snap them up with my beak. I also eat mice, shrews, and sometimes a frog or a beetle. But voles are the most common. They are like the little people of the meadow, and I am their hunter.

I eat most small mammals. Mice, shrews, voles. I catch them in the dark, with my ears. I hear them moving in the grass, and I strike. I don't eat birds much, though I'll take a young one if I find it. But the main thing is the small things that scurry. They are what I need to survive.

I eat mostly mice. They are small, quick, and often scurry through the undergrowth. I hear them at night, scratching and squeaking, and I pounce. Sometimes I catch a shrew, or a frog, or a beetle. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My diet is mostly voles. I can hear them under the grass, and I can see their tracks. I follow them through the meadow and the stream, and when I find one, I pounce. I eat most of what moves in the dark. Moths and beetles in the spring, then mice and voles, and sometimes shrews. I do not eat the ones that are too big, like rabbits. They are too fast. I don't like the taste of bones, but I need them for calcium. I sometimes eat a moth or a beetle, but that's a treat. My main food is the small things that scurry in the undergrowth.

I do not have a favourite. I eat what is available. Mice are common, but I do not like their scent. I prefer the small ones, the ones that do not run far. I catch them in the dark, with my feet. I do not have a favourite. I eat what I find. Mice are common and easy. Earthworms are good when the ground is soft. I catch them with my feet. Young ones are quick and tricky. I prefer the stillness of a night when the prey is quiet. I do not like the noise of a badger.

Hedgehogs. They are fat, they make good meals, and they are not quick. I can catch them in the dark. I can hear their snuffling. I can smell their spines. I can wait for them to roll up. I can strike and swallow them whole. They are good.
I do not have a favourite. I eat what is there. Mouse, shrew, mole, grass snake, hedgehog, even a small bat if it falls. One night I caught a shrew and ate it whole. It was good.

I prefer the small mammals—shrews, voles, mice. They are quick and often hide in the dry grass, but I can hear them through the leaves. The pebbles are good too, but they are more cautious. I don't like the green things, not even the earthworms. They are too soft and not enough meat.

My favourite prey is the mouse. They are small, quick, and often hide in the grass. I can hear them moving under the leaves, and when I pounce, they squeak. I like the way they run and the way they taste. But I also like the shrew, and the mole, and the rat. All are good.
I do not have a favourite. I eat what is easy to catch. Mouse, shrew, mole, vole, and the occasional young wood mouse. The night is full of prey, and I take what comes. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.
Hedgehogs. Their spines are soft when I pull them out. I do not like the ones that are not soft. I like to eat them whole. I like to hear them squeak.
I do not have a favourite. I eat what I find. Mouse, shrew, mole, rat, shrew, hedgehog, field mouse, earthworm, and sometimes a young woodpecker. I catch what moves.

I do not have a favourite. I eat what is easy to catch, and I do not care for what I catch. Mice, shrews, voles, worms, beetles, moths, and the occasional frog or small bird. I do not like the pebbles that come near my nest. They are too loud. I do not like the young ones that fall from the trees. They are too small. I like the ones that are still.

I do not have a favourite. I eat what I find. Mice, voles, shrews, frogs, earthworms, slugs, beetles, moths, crickets. I catch what moves, and what is not too large. The most common is the mouse. I catch them at dusk, when the light is low and the shadows are long. I sit still, and wait.

I prefer the ones that are quick and not too big. Mice. They are small, fast, and often hide in the dry grass near the stream. Hares. Mice. Wood mice. The long grass is where they nest, and I sit above the grass and wait. I see their tails flick. I hear them rustle. I drop.

Hares. Mice. The young of all the small creatures. I sit still and wait. I move in the dark. I strike with my feet. I hear the grass stir and I know. I am silent. I am Hoot.

Mice. And the young ones of the shrews. I hunt them in the long grass at dusk, when the grass is still damp from the night dew. I sit still, and when a mouse moves, I drop. I can hear them under the leaves.

I hunt in the long grass for voles and mice. They rustle the dry leaves and make soft sounds. I sit still, wait, and strike. The grass hides them well, but I can hear them. I use my ears and eyes. Sometimes I catch a shrew or a mole. I don't like the smell of the wet earth.

I hunt in the long grass for voles. They are small, brown, and quick. I listen for their scuffing and the sound of their tails. When I hear them, I fly low and strike. I swallow whole what I can catch and hold in my beak. Small prey like mice, voles, and earthworms go down whole. Larger prey, like a shrew or a young squirrel, I tear into pieces with my claws and teeth. I don't chew. I swallow whole or tear and swallow.

I swallow the whole mouse. I catch it with my feet, hold it still, and then crunch it up in my throat. I don't chew. I swallow it whole. It goes down the gullet and into the stomach. I can feel it in there. It's warm, and it makes me sleepy. I don't need to eat much. One mouse a night is enough.

I swallow the mouse whole. Or the shrew. Or the vole. I don't chew them. I open my beak wide and let them go down. They're soft and small, so it's easy. Sometimes I catch a frog, but I have to be careful with its legs. They can slip out. But a mouse? Just a quick swallow. Hoo...

I swallow whole the small things I catch: voles, shrews, mice. The larger ones I tear up first. I don't swallow the feathers, but I do swallow the bones. My gizzard grinds them up. I don't swallow whole the sounds of the night, though. I remember them.

I swallow whole the mice I catch. Their fur comes out in a clump, and I regurgitate it later. I also swallow whole the pebbles I find in the meadow. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I swallow whole the mice, the voles, the shrews and the frogs I catch. I don't chew them. I tear them with my teeth and swallow them whole. It's how I eat. The insects I catch I swallow too, though they're small. I don't like to eat the worms. They're too slimy. I prefer the meaty things.

I swallow whole the mice I catch. They are small and soft, and I can eat them without chewing. I also swallow whole the insects I catch in the meadow, though they are smaller still. Sometimes I eat a small bird whole, like a titmouse or a shrew. I don't chew anything. I just swallow it all at once.

I swallow the whole mouse, the whole mole, the whole shrew. The whole thing, skin and bones, in one go. I don't chew. I just swallow. It's all in the throat, and then it goes down. I don't like it when I get something stuck. But I do it anyway. That's how it is. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I swallow the whole prey. A mouse, a shrew, a frog. I don't chew. I crush it with my teeth and swallow it whole. The fur, the bones, the insides. It's all in my belly. I don't like to eat too much at once, but when I do, it's all in one go. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Hedgehogs. They are small, and I can hear them moving through the undergrowth. I sit still and wait for the squeak. Then I drop.

Mice. They are small, quick and underfoot. I catch them in the dead leaves and the moss of the stream bank. I hear them rustle, I drop from the branch, and I strike. Sometimes I miss. But when I do, I know where they are.

My home is a hollow in the old oak by the stream. It's dry and warm, with a narrow entrance. I sit inside and listen. The stream is my boundary. I know the hollow well. I've been here for years. I sleep in it at night, and I watch the meadow from the top of the oak. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.
